solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tradesman possibly welcomed by the three blind mice?

blocks.note: surface reading: a shopkeeper who sells goods to the public

blocks.clueFragment: welcomed by the three blind mice
blocks.note: setter's reading: the mice lost their tails to the farmer's wife, so someone who could give them tails again would be most welcome

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as RE-TAILER, one who tails again. In the nursery rhyme the farmer's wife cut off the tails of the three blind mice with a carving knife.
explanation.definitionFit: A retailer is a shopkeeper selling goods directly to customers, which is one kind of tradesman.

clue.text: Dog reportedly moves unsteadily? It’s the tummy trouble

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we want a word that sounds like this one

blocks.note: a collie is a sheepdog
to wobble is to move unsteadily from side to side

explanation.surface: A dog staggering about, and the cause turns out to be an upset stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the dog is the sound-alike: COLLIE is spelt COLLY, then WOBBLES is added as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Collywobbles is an informal word for stomach pain or queasiness, often brought on by nerves.

clue.text: Language used by Sheba’s queen?

indicators.note: the letters are put to use within the following words, sitting there ready to be lifted out

blocks.note: the run of letters straddles the three words

explanation.surface: Asks what tongue the biblical Queen of Sheba spoke.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across sheBA'S QUEen, ignoring the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Basque is the ancient non-Indo-European tongue spoken in the western Pyrenees of Spain and France.

clue.text: Standards identified by exam in writing

indicators.note: one thing set inside another is in it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: an oral is a spoken examination
MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Academic standards being measured by a written exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exam in writing' reads like a written test, but the spoken exam goes inside the manuscript abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Morals are principles of right conduct, the ethical standards by which a person lives.

clue.text: Benevolent type

blocks.note: first meaning: generous and caring towards others
second meaning: a sort or category

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase, a charitable person, but splits into an adjective and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for generous goodwill and a noun meaning a sort or class.

clue.text: Extremely fashionable woman’s soft brimmed hat

indicators.note: extremes are the far ends, so only the outermost letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: its first and last letters
Dora is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A stylish woman wearing a soft hat with a brim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely fashionable' looks like high praise, but it takes only the ends of the word. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is a felt hat with a creased crown and a soft, flexible brim.

clue.text: Source of old gear at home

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a rig is a set of equipment
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: Where someone's old kit came from: it was in the house all along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old gear' is one picture in the surface but two separate pieces in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An origin is the point where something begins or comes from, the same as its source.

clue.text: Establishment in railway property everyone enters

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a station is a building belonging to the railway
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A business set up on railway land that everybody walks into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word placing the establishment, but it supplies its own two letters at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An installation is a military or industrial base or facility, which is one meaning of establishment.

clue.text: Bar on cricket pitch sometimes jumped by miscreants?

blocks.note: first meaning: one of the two small wooden crosspieces resting on the stumps
second meaning: release money that offenders forfeit when they abscond

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bails sit across the top of the stumps. To jump bail is to fail to appear in court after being released.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a wicket crosspiece in cricket and also the security deposit that lets an accused person await trial outside prison.

clue.text: Crucial-sounding team in dock area

indicators.note: a word that sounds like another is said the same, so the spelling changes but not the sound

blocks.note: something crucial is key
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: An important team playing near the docks.
explanation.walkthrough: KEY and QUAY are said the same in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: The quayside is the waterfront strip beside a wharf where ships moor and are loaded.

clue.text: Perfect films regularly shown around various parts of Wales

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept
various pieces put together any old how means the letters are rearranged
to go around something is to enclose it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Flawless films being screened at intervals across Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various parts of Wales' sounds like a touring route, but it rearranges the letters of the country's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Flawless means without any defect or blemish, which is exactly what perfect describes.

clue.text: Prosecute university in the Home Counties

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for university
the Home Counties surround London in south-east England, SE

explanation.surface: Taking legal action against a university near London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London, so they stand for the south-east, SE.
explanation.definitionFit: To sue is to bring a legal action against someone, a close equivalent of prosecuting them.

clue.text: Cunning, avoiding start of demonstration

indicators.note: steering clear of the beginning means the opening letter is left off

blocks.note: a march is a protest demonstration, here losing its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone sly enough to dodge the beginning of a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demonstration' is not a display but a protest march.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch as an adjective means knowing, sly or mischievous, a sense close to cunning.

clue.text: Meet first of chums on border

indicators.note: the first of something is its opening, so only the initial letter is kept

blocks.note: its first letter
taken as written
a verge is a grassy border along a road

explanation.surface: Meeting the first of your friends at the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' is not placing one piece after another; it is two letters of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To converge is to come together from different directions, which is what meeting involves.

clue.text: Hired vehicle carrying last of popular seafood

indicators.note: the last of something is its tail end, so only the final letter is kept
to carry something is to hold it, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: a cab is a taxi, a vehicle for hire
its final letter

explanation.surface: A taxi transporting a load of a much-liked seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Popular seafood' reads as one phrase, but only the final letter of 'popular' is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Crab is a shellfish eaten widely, a typical example of seafood.

clue.text: Girl scoffing second pudding

indicators.note: to scoff is to gobble food down, so one piece swallows the other

blocks.note: Selina is a girl's name
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A girl wolfing down a second helping of dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second pudding' looks like a second helping, but 'second' is MO, British slang for a moment, as in 'half a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: Semolina pudding, made from wheat grains boiled in milk, is a classic British school dessert.

clue.text: Break in school is marvellous to begin with

indicators.note: what comes to begin with is the opening, so only the initial letter is kept

blocks.note: SCH is the abbreviation for school
taken as written
its first letter

explanation.surface: A pupil enthusing that break time is marvellous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break in school' suggests playtime, but 'Break' alone is the definition, in the sense of a split.
explanation.definitionFit: A schism is a split or division within a group, especially a church, so a break between factions.

clue.text: This person’s outstanding, cutting old woman’s shrub

indicators.note: something that cuts into another goes inside it, splitting it apart

blocks.note: this person is the setter, so 'this person is' becomes I'M
o/s is the accounting abbreviation for outstanding, as in an unpaid bill
ma is an informal word for one's mother, an old woman

explanation.surface: A gardener boasting about trimming an elderly lady's bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old woman' is slang for mother, MA, which the other two pieces split. 'Outstanding' means owed, not excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimosa is a flowering bush or small tree with fluffy yellow blooms, an acacia.

clue.text: Oddly, a shy male terrier

indicators.note: acting oddly means behaving out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A timid male dog behaving strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' could suggest taking odd letters, but there are exactly eight letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sealyham is a small white Welsh breed of terrier, named after a house in Pembrokeshire.

clue.text: Style and vigour a large antelope mostly shows

indicators.note: most but not all of something means the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a large African antelope, here losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A big antelope displaying grace and energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' belongs with the antelope, not with the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is energetic flair and dash, a close match for style combined with vigour.

clue.text: Youngster finally taken by supporter on course

indicators.note: what comes finally comes at the end, so only the last letter is kept

blocks.note: a tee is the peg supporting a golf ball on the course
its final letter

explanation.surface: A young player being picked up by a fan at the racecourse or golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' suggests a fan, but on a golf course it is the peg the ball sits on.
explanation.definitionFit: A teen is a teenager, a young person aged thirteen to nineteen.

clue.text: Sailor’s useless ankle or heel bone

blocks.note: a tar is a sailor
U/S is short for unserviceable, useless

explanation.surface: A sailor complaining that an injured ankle or heel is no good.
explanation.walkthrough: U/S, unserviceable, is British service slang for broken or useless.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarsus is the group of bones forming the ankle, including the heel bone, in anatomy.

clue.text: Like loofahs perhaps ultimately emitting unpleasant odour

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter is kept

blocks.note: its final letter
pongy is British slang for smelly, from pong, a stink

explanation.surface: Old bath loofahs that have started to smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' looks like it hedges the definition, but it supplies only its last letter. A pong is a bad smell in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofah is a dried gourd used as a bath sponge, so it is soft, porous and absorbent.
